question_text: Why is gypsum added to cement?

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What is added
lines: About 2 – 3% of it by weight is ground
steps.why: The answer opens with what gypsum is and how much of it goes in, because the amount is small and deliberate. Gypsum is added to the clinker at the grinding stage; it is not one of the raw materials burnt in the kiln.
common_mistakes: Writing the half water molecule, CaSO₄·½H₂O. What is ground with the clinker is the dihydrate, with two water molecules.
Adding the gypsum before burning. It is ground with the clinker after the burning is over.
steps.memory_tip: Gypsum, two waters, two to three per cent, added at the grinding stage.
steps.margin_note: Give the formula and the percentage before giving the reason.

steps.label: The reason
lines: Gypsum slows down the setting of the
Without it the cement paste would set
too quickly to be mixed and placed.
The slower setting lets the cement
harden properly into a strong mass.
steps.why: Gypsum controls the rate at which cement reacts with water. The setting still takes place; it is delayed, and that delay is what gives time to place the cement and lets it gain its full strength.
common_mistakes: Writing that gypsum stops the cement from setting. It slows the setting, it does not prevent it.
Writing that gypsum makes the cement set faster. Its effect is the opposite.
steps.memory_tip: Gypsum slows the setting; it does not stop it.
steps.margin_note: Use the word slows. Setting is delayed, not prevented.

insider_note: One word carries this answer — gypsum slows the setting — and a complete answer also says why a slower set is useful.
